All support would be greatly appreciated GAA House Draw Waterford GAA has launched its third Winner House Draw to support the next phase of the major €16.2 million redevelopment of Azzurri Walsh Park. Phase two is expected to move to contract shortly, with a Waterford-based contractor selected and work due to begin in the coming weeks. More than €10.4 million in Government and Immigrant Inve stor Programme funding has already been secured, with Waterford GAA aiming to raise approximately five per cent of the overall redevelopment cost through the house draw. Ferrybank GAA are selling tickets for the draw and, importantly, the club will receive a rebate for every ticket purchased through them. Supporters are therefore encouraged to buy their tickets directly from Ferrybank GAA, helping both the Walsh Park redevelopment and the local club. Tickets are priced at €50 for one, €80 for two or €100 f or three, with a house as the main prize, along with a few smaller prizes throughout the year. Ferrybank GAA will hold the Annual General Meeting on Wednesday, November 25th at 7.30 pm in the New Clubhouse. All membe rs are strongly encouraged to attend and take an active interest in the running and future developme nt of the club. The continued success of Ferrybank GAA depends on the involvement and support of members, and the AGM provides an important opportunity for everyone to contribute. Please make every effort to attend. A good turnout is important for the future of the club. Roman Catholic Diocese and Parishes of Ossory - Regd. Charity No. 20015831 The Feast of Christ The King This Sunday, the final Sunday of the Church’s year, we celebrate the Feast of Christ the King. But Christ is a King unlike any other. His throne was a cross, His crown was made of thorns, and His power was expressed through love, mercy and forgiveness. In a world often divided by conflict, selfishness and the pursuit of power, Christ reminds us that true greatness is found in serving others. As we ap- proach Advent, may we allow Christ to reign in our hearts, our homes and our communities, bringing His peace and compassion into everyday life. We continue during this month of November to remember in our Masses and Prayers our deceased loved ones who have died.
Thoughts on Grief … Cardinal Basil Hume, OSB Grief cannot be shared, for it is mine alone.
Grief is dying within me, a great emptiness, a frightening void.
It is loneliness, a sickening sorrow at night, on awakening a terrible dread.
Another’s words do not help. A reasoned argument explains little for having tried too much.
Silence is the best response to anothe r’s grief.
Not the silence that is a pause in speech, awkward and unwanted, but one that unites heart to heart.
Love, speaking in silence, is the way into the void of another’s grief.
